title: Load Test Simulator — Find the Knee of the Curve
description: A clearly labelled, seeded discrete-event model of a fictional service. Set the workers, service-time distribution, client timeout, queue limit, autoscaling and a slow leak, then drive it with ramp-up, steady, spike or soak virtual-user profiles. Watch requests flow through the queue while live charts plot throughput, users, p50/p95/p99 latency and error rate, and a knee chart marks where extra users stop adding throughput and start adding latency, next to the N* saturation estimate.
prompt: Build 'Load Test Simulator': a clearly labelled queueing model of a fictional service, with c workers, a service-time distribution, a timeout and an autoscaling toggle. Let me define a virtual-user profile (ramp-up, steady, spike, soak) and watch requests flow, with live charts of throughput, active users, p50/p95/p99 latency computed from the simulated samples, and error rate. Help me find the knee of the curve. It must be seeded so tests are deterministic. Make it look like an industrial control panel: gunmetal, safety orange, condensed type.

methodology: Analytical oracles: capacity c ÷ S and the closed-system saturation estimate N* = c·(S + Z) ÷ S are asserted exactly, and the measured knee of a seeded ramp must land in a band around N*.
Invariant checks rather than magic numbers: p50 ≤ p95 ≤ p99, successful latencies never exceed the client timeout, and peak throughput stays below capacity plus window noise.
Determinism: the same seed and settings reproduce an identical summary after reset, and a different seed produces a different run, which proves the PRNG really drives the model.

Comparative (metamorphic) tests: tripling the workers removes errors and lowers p95; turning on autoscaling under steady overload raises the final worker count and total throughput; a spike against a tight timeout produces errors.
Real-time path: page.clock drives the requestAnimationFrame loop, so simulated time advances by exactly speed × elapsed, and pausing freezes it.
risks: Canvas drawing with NaN values from empty windows (percentiles of zero samples); every coordinate goes through a finite guard.
Event-ordering ties between a request finishing and its timeout at the same instant; the heap breaks ties by insertion order.
Retiring virtual users when the profile drops (spike end) must not leak in-flight counters or keep sending.
Performance of a 15-minute soak at high user counts when finished instantly.
qa.playwright: All randomness flows from a mulberry32 PRNG seeded by ?seed= or the seed field, and the whole simulation can be run to completion synchronously with Finish, so most tests never wait on animation. The summary exposes raw numbers as data-* attributes, which tests compare as numbers, including a deep-equality check between two runs. For the animated path, page.clock.install plus pauseAt freezes time before load; runFor(2000) then steps the rAF loop deterministically and the simulated clock is asserted to be about 20 s at 10× speed. Charts are canvas and are not pixel-diffed; their inputs are covered through the summary and the knee attribute instead.
coverage: Capacity and N* readouts react to workers and think time; profile durations
Seeded ramp: invariants, knee in range, reproducibility and seed sensitivity
More workers: no errors, lower p95, no knee
Spike with a tight timeout; autoscaling adds workers
Live animation under page.clock, pause and finish

a11y: Every setting is a labelled native control with a live <output>, the profiles are aria-pressed buttons, and each canvas has an accessible name, with the same numbers also given as text in the summary and knee sentence. Reduced-motion users get twice-a-second updates instead of per-frame animation.
